doors.title: I'm new to this
doors.sub: Six short paths, in order. Each one ends with something you can picture and explain.

doors.title: I design systems
doors.sub: Say what you are building. Get the lesson to watch, the gate to run, the playbook and a worked example.

doors.title: Explore freely
doors.sub: The living map, the two atlas lessons, the stack, the questions people ask. Go anywhere; progress is kept.

paths.title: What AI is, really
paths.promise: You can say what makes a system 'AI', where machine learning and language models sit inside it, and why the data it learned from matters.

stops.label: The stack in seven layers
stops.sub: Every AI word you have heard lives in exactly one of them.

paths.title: How a machine learns
paths.promise: You can follow one model from raw text to a released version, and explain what training actually changes.

stops.label: Follow one model from text to release
stops.sub: The second atlas lesson. Fifteen steps; try the three ways it can be held back.

paths.title: What a language model does
paths.promise: You can explain tokens, context and attention well enough to know why a model forgets, drifts and sometimes makes things up.

stops.label: Watch a model propose, not act
stops.sub: Step 5 of the flagship lesson, then follow the run to the end.

paths.title: What makes it an agent
paths.promise: You can tell a model, a chatbot, a workflow and an agent apart, and describe the loop an agent runs.

stops.label: Model, chatbot, workflow, agent
stops.sub: Four kinds that get called the same thing.

stops.label: Follow one request through a governed system
stops.sub: The flagship lesson, start to verified completion.

paths.title: Running it safely
paths.promise: You can name what stops an agent doing harm, and tell a prompt from a rule.

stops.label: A prompt is a request. A check in code is a rule.
Watch a refund get denied before execution
stops.sub: The gate refuses; the run ends as denied, not failed.

stops.label: Watch a planted instruction get blocked
stops.sub: The model follows it; the check in code does not.

paths.title: Should we build one?
paths.promise: You can run the questions that decide whether an agent is the right call, and name the gates it has to pass.

stops.label: Four questions decide it
stops.sub: Most teams should answer 'not yet' to the last one.

stops.label: The autonomy ladder
stops.sub: Five rungs. Each one needs more of the estate underneath it.

stops.label: The eight gates
stops.sub: Between a demo and a system.

stops.label: Run the gate check
stops.sub: Score a system you know against the eight gates.
